title: Condensation is water vapor turning back into liquid
summary: Condensation is water vapor turning into liquid water, which is why a cold glass grows wet on the outside on a humid day.
body: The U.S. Geological Survey says condensation changes gaseous water into liquid water, and that it is the opposite of evaporation. The page points at water on the outside of a cold glass on a humid day. It also says the air is full of water vapor even when we cannot see it, and that condensation builds clouds. Fog at ground level, a cold window, and the inside of a car window after people have been breathing moist air are further examples of vapor leaving warm air and becoming liquid as it cools. Cloud droplets and rain are a later step, not this card.
